bluf: Junto is a Paris performance agency of 80+ people, founded 2016, that sells paid media first and bundles SEO, tracking, creative strategy and CRM into one AI first offer it calls Junto ONE. The record shows it claiming 800+ clients since 2016, publishing at pace (732 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days) and adding a ChatGPT Ads page for early entry into OpenAI's ad format. The Horus read is Neutral at 7.1, best placed for the click giving way to the citation. A rival should know all 30 clients on record are names only and two sold lines fail their own house tests.
doing:
The positioning line reads: the sharp growth team of French market leaders, unifying paid media, SEO, tracking, creative strategy and CRM in one AI first offer. In plain words: a paid media shop that has wrapped the adjacent lines into a single retainer and put AI on the label. The headline claim is volume plus one number: 800+ clients since 2016, 200+ growth references, and a Yellowpop case reporting revenue up 1,274% in a year.

The services list runs from Paid Media & Ads and programmatic to SEO, GEO, tracking, CRO, creative, video, CRM, growth and B2B lead gen. The lead lines at 3 are Paid Search (lever one of Junto ONE; the ads page claims the reference Paid Media firm) and Paid Social (OpenClassrooms LinkedIn CPL cut fivefold; Leocare paid social doubled revenue). Core lines at 2 are AI Automation / Agents (AI lead scoring, AI driven CRM workflows), AI Search / GEO (a GEO page targeting ChatGPT, Perplexity and Copilot citations; 48 AI URLs), B2B & ABM (the OpenClassrooms ABM case), Data & Measurement (GA4 audits, server side tracking), Email & CRM (lead scoring, nurturing, a HubSpot CRM page), Programmatic & CTV (Amazon DSP, DV360; the Airton DOOH case) and SEO (14 sub service URLs). Proprietary names: Junto ONE (run via Groupe Blueland) and an unnamed data platform that audits client measurement.

The AI posture is AI first by brand: AI scoring, CRM workflows and content across services, GEO for LLM citations and an early ChatGPT Ads offer.

The one move carries no date: a ChatGPT Ads service page pitching early entry into OpenAI's conversational ad format. Pricing signals: free creative audit, growth audits and strategy consultations, no prices shown. It also sells a media training catalogue. Conspicuously absent: any platform partner badge, any dated move, jobs, news, and a described case for any of its 30 named clients.
clients:
The Radar files the client type as mixed, the home market as France from a Paris office, and the verticals as E-commerce, SaaS & software, B2B lead gen, D2C / DNVB, Retail & omnichannel, Mobile apps, Finance & insurance, Education & edtech, Fashion & luxury, Automotive, Real estate and Health & wellness. The needs read counts 30 clients and observes a need for none (15 case study pages, 15 slugs), so the mix read is empty.

The case study names are OpenClassrooms, Getfluence, Qonto, Leocare, Yellowpop, GSK, Preply, Dalloz, BMW Motorrad Équipement, Pretto, Direct Emploi, StudentJob, Smartrental, Coiff&Co and Sisters Republic; the slugs add PwC, BMW, Mirakl, Pennylane, Livestorm, Sciences Po, Swissquote, Franprix, Decathlon, Vestiaire Collective, OVHcloud, Air Liquide, Delsey, École Polytechnique and EDHEC to the list. The needs read files every one as named only, but the capability notes describe work for three: OpenClassrooms (LinkedIn CPL cut fivefold, an ABM case) reads as B2B pipeline and paid performance, Leocare (paid social doubled revenue) and Yellowpop (revenue up 1,274%) as paid performance. Every other need is inferred from the sold mix, paid media first.

Four are shared with other tracked agencies: Preply with kaizen and jbh, Decathlon with epsilon and valtech, PwC and Air Liquide with eskimoz. The whole book is names only (30 of 30).

What the base needs next: KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) and KJ2 (ads inside AI answers scale faster than any channel before them) are its tailwinds, so it is likely, moderate confidence, that its SaaS and ecommerce clients are sold GEO and ChatGPT Ads tests on top of paid media; KJ5 (the price of attention splits in two) is its headwind through paid social and programmatic, so those budgets are a roughly even chance to be repriced within the edition.
house: Say and do: 2 of 4 tested lines are practised on its own house. Publishing cadence is corroborated and heavy: 732 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days and 919 in 365, from a sitemap of 1,676, with 48 AI topic URLs. LinkedIn advertising is corroborated: 8 company page ads as a floor, from 365 ads matching the name query; one checked ad paid for by Junto SAS ran 9 to 22 July 2026, and a sample in French asks whether the reader spends hours generating leads that are not qualified and struggle to sign. AI Search / GEO is contradicted: it sells AI visibility and publishes no llms.txt. Paid social is contradicted: it sells paid social and runs no social ad pixel on its own site. Paid search is unknown because the Transparency Center lookup was blocked. The tag stack is GTM and Didomi on Next.js with Storyblok; no test tools or ABM stack are listed.
market:
The Horus read scores a tailwind index of 7.1, Neutral band. It is best placed for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation, net 0.219), driven by AI Search / GEO, and for KJ2 (ads inside AI answers scale faster than any channel before them, net 0.182). It is most exposed to KJ5 (the price of attention splits in two, net -0.141) through Paid Social and Programmatic & CTV, and to KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer) through Paid Search and Paid Social. Best fit is The Bazaar of Agents at 38/100. The read has it making P4, P7 and P8 (ads inside assistants with holdout measurement), partial on P1 and P6, unknown on P5, absent on P2, P3 not applicable.

The Monsoon read scores 48.6, Breeze band: migration 47.1 against displacement 50.1; SEO (8) and Paid Search (8) carry the most movable hours. The work would go 45% to Africa and the Maghreb, 30% to South and Southeast Asia and 20% to Eastern Europe. No hub office and no onshore claim are listed, footprint inferred.
openings:
Lead with the contradictions. It sells AI visibility with 48 AI topic URLs and no llms.txt, and paid social with no social pixel; a rival whose house passes both puts the gap on one slide; very likely, high confidence, it lands with clients buying GEO on trust. The falsifier is an llms.txt and a social pixel appearing on junto.fr.

Second, the empty book: 30 names and no described case, with the results that exist (OpenClassrooms, Leocare, Yellowpop) living in notes rather than case pages. A rival with written French cases can ask a prospect to name a Junto result; likely, moderate confidence. The shared clients are the first calls: Preply (kaizen, jbh), Decathlon (epsilon, valtech), PwC and Air Liquide (eskimoz) are already multi agency.

Third, it sells GEO with no audited AI visibility product (P1 partial), so citation share and a scorecard beat the page. Fourth, no feed, schema or entity work (P2 absent) leaves the machine readable layer unclaimed. Fifth, price: no public model (P5 unknown) leaves an outcome priced offer open. The ChatGPT Ads line is unlikely to be contestable head on: P8 is marked making with holdout measurement, so a rival must show results, not intent.
watch: I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, next reading late October 2026: search and other growth below 10% flags cannibalisation of its paid search lead line; above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and its KJ1 tailwind.
I10, Reddit US daily users versus search referral volatility, next reading late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk behind KJ1.
I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the next milestone ($2B) and pricing below $20 CPM would decide whether its early ChatGPT Ads offer is a tailwind or a cost centre.
I4, Meta Q3 2026 average price per ad, next reading late October 2026: a print at or above +5% continues walled garden inflation and deepens its KJ5 exposure through paid social.
The undated ChatGPT Ads page: a dated case or result with holdouts would turn the P8 move from claim to proof and close the strongest counter pitch.
The next Radar compile: the dossier is only as fresh as 28 September 2026, and a new compile refreshes offices, ads, sitemap cadence and clients.
